title: U.S. House · Michigan's 11th District
area: Oakland County, including Southfield, Troy, Farmington Hills and surrounding suburbs.

context.text: This is an open seat with no incumbent on the ballot. Democratic state Sen. Jeremy Moss and Republican former Troy Mayor Ethan Baker advanced from contested primaries.

candidates.name: Jeremy Moss
candidates.currentRole: Michigan State Senator, District 7 (not seeking re-election to that seat)

priorities.text: Lowering healthcare costs and restoring federal Medicaid and SNAP funding.
priorities.quote: In the State Senate, I protected Michigan from the harshest cuts by restoring funding to Medicaid and SNAP, and enshrined Obamacare in state law when it was under attack in Washington... I strongly support a robust public option as a pathway to universal coverage.

priorities.text: Addressing the cost of living, including housing, tariffs and corporate price gouging.
priorities.quote: We are facing an affordability crisis, from groceries and gas to healthcare and childcare... Congress must overturn the devastating impacts of Trump's big awful bill that have increased costs on Michigan families.

priorities.text: Overhauling federal immigration enforcement while securing the border.
priorities.quote: The cruelty and chaos caused by ICE cannot be repaired or reformed under Donald Trump and the agency must be dismantled... We can both secure our border without allowing officers posing as masked vigilantes to erode due process and civil liberties.

positions.summary: Supports a robust public option as a pathway to universal healthcare coverage.
positions.quote: I strongly support a robust public option as a pathway to universal coverage.

positions.summary: Opposes the Trump administration's tariff policy, saying it has raised consumer prices.
positions.quote: Stopping the chaotic tariff policy: Michigan's economy depends on stable supply chains and strong international partnerships. A tariff policy that changes by the month has only raised prices for consumers and hurt workers and small businesses.

positions.summary: Says ICE should be dismantled and reformed, and supports legal pathways to citizenship for DACA recipients and long-term undocumented residents, while saying the border should still be secured.
positions.quote: We must create legal pathways to citizenship for those protected under DACA and for undocumented immigrants with long-standing ties to the US.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to pre-K and Head Start programs.
positions.quote: Investing in pre-K and headstart programs: Families should not have to choose between paying the bills and caring for their children. Expanding access to pre-K and Head Start programs would give every child a strong foundation for success.

positions.summary: Cosponsored and voted yes on SB 76 (requiring a license or background check to purchase a firearm), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-17 on 2023-03-16.
Voted yes on SB 8 (raising Michigan's minimum wage to $15 by 2027 and phasing in a higher tipped minimum wage), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-12 on 2025-02-13.

record.text: Chairs the Michigan Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Regulatory Reform Committee for the 2025-2026 session; also serves on the Economic and Small Business Development and Local Government committees.
Cosponsored and voted yes on SB 76 (requiring a license or background check to purchase a firearm), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-17 on 2023-03-16.
Voted yes on SB 8 (raising Michigan's minimum wage to $15 by 2027 and phasing in a higher tipped minimum wage for restaurant workers), which passed the Michigan Senate 20-12 on 2025-02-13.

candidates.researchNotes: Birth year is not given in the sources reviewed.

candidates.name: Ethan Baker

priorities.text: Says he is running to reduce political division and bring a more respectful, solutions-focused tone to Congress.
priorities.quote: The issues we're facing—cost of living, economic uncertainty, local jobs, infrastructure, our mental and physical health, and safety at home and abroad—need to be addressed now and are too important to be handled through division alone.

record.text: Served as Mayor of Troy, Michigan.
Served as chair and U.S. Commissioner for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission.

candidates.researchNotes: Baker's campaign website statement quoted by Ballotpedia focuses on tone and bipartisanship rather than specific policy positions; no statements matching the guide's fixed issue list were found. Baker's Troy mayoral and Great Lakes roles are as described on his campaign website and Ballotpedia; no independent news profile was reviewed.

candidates.name: Ryan Teasdale

priorities.text: Public safety, mental health, affordable housing and development, and government and corporate transparency as primary focus areas.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website lists four focus areas (public safety; mental health; affordable housing and development; government and corporate transparency) without policy positions. No questionnaire or debate coverage found. Biography draws on Ballotpedia and his self-written survey; no campaign website or news profile was found.

candidates.name: Farid Ishac
candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website, platform or questionnaire found; BallotReady lists LinkedIn only and Ballotpedia shows no 2026 survey response. Biography draws on Ballotpedia and a 2024 candidate survey; no campaign website or news profile was found.

candidates.name: Anil Kumar

priorities.text: Healthcare reform that puts patients before profit.
priorities.quote: fighting for healthcare reform that puts patients before profit, for educational opportunity that lifts every family
